title: Runbook stitching & dependency handover protocol (pilot)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working pilot to standardize how runbooks are stitched together across teams and how ownership of downstream dependencies transfers during SLO-focused launch cutovers and incident escalations. The goal is to reduce handoff friction, eliminate single-team blind spots, and make rollback/mitigation faster when a dependency fails.

Scope (pilot):
- Services: model-serving mesh (inference-gateway, kv-cache, routing), batching service, metrics-exporter, and the platform VPN connector.
- Teams: serving-runtime, infra, platform-engineering, observability, product-hosted-api, eng-sre.
- Workstreams: runbook templates, dependency matrix, handover play, sprint-run validation, incident drills.
- Out of scope: on-prem packaging changes, billing integration (handled by finance ops).

Why this differs from prior SLO docs:
- Focused on "stitching" documents (runbooks/playbooks) so an operator following a single doc can call out to a clear next-step owner with context, not just a stub link.
- Formal handover protocol that defines responsibility shifts during degraded operation windows (canary cutover, model swap, cache invalidation).
- Lightweight automation hooks: link IDs, runbook anchors, and runbook-aware Slack shortcuts to spin up a collaboration channel.

Stakeholders and RACI (high-level):
- eng-sre (Asha Patel) - accountable for the protocol and pilot coordination.
- serving-runtime (Jonah Kim) - responsible for runbook content for model-serving components.
- observability (Evelyn Park) - responsible for alert mapping and SLI/SLO verification steps.
- platform-engineering (Marco Diaz) - responsible for infra-level mitigation scripts and runbook fragments exposing runbook endpoints.
- product-hosted-api (Priya Singh) - consulted for customer-impact assessment and SLA communications.

Success measures (pilot):
- Drill time-to-mitigation reduces by 25% vs baseline (baseline: mean of last 6 drills).
- 90% of runbook transitions include a clear next owner + contact and expected TTR windows.
- No critical blindspots discovered in dependency matrix (>=95% of dependencies mapped).

Artifacts to produce:
- Runbook stitching template (markdown with anchors + callout sections).
- Dependency matrix CSV (service, repo, owner, contact, fallback).
- Handover checklist snippet (short, 8 steps max) that fits into a page.
- Slack shortcut: /handover-start that posts runbook anchor and creates ephemeral channel.

Pilot timeline (8 weeks):
- Week 0 (planning, owner alignment): finalize scope, owners, and core template (owner: Asha)
- Week 1-2 (content capture): serving-runtime and obs fill runbook fragments for target services
- Week 3 (stitching): infra and platform engineerers map automation hooks and anchors; create dependency matrix draft
- Week 4 (validation): dry-run with simulated incident (no customer impact) + time-to-mitigation measurement
- Week 5 (retro + iterate): update runbooks + checklist based on drill notes
- Week 6 (wider rollouts): invite product-hosted-api and a customer-success rep to review communications steps
- Week 7-8 (buffer): fix gaps, prepare final pilot report and recommendations for org-wide pattern

Example handover checklist (short):
1) Confirm incident scope and affected SLO(s).
2) Post runbook anchor and open /handover channel (include incident id).
3) Identify upstream and downstream owners from dependency matrix.
4) Assign initial mitigation lead (15-min ownership window).
5) Execute immediate mitigations (listed in runbook).
6) Validate SLIs and update incident channel with timestamped checks.
7) If mitigation requires cross-team change, execute formal handover: assign new owner + expected SLA for action.
8) If no progress within escalation window, escalate to SRE on-call + exec liaison.

Guidelines for runbook fragments (serving-runtime example):
- Keep each fragment < 800 words. Prefer checklist bullets.
- Provide exact CLI/console commands and expected result lines to match observability metrics.
- Include a short rollback plan with TEST/VERIFY steps.
- Anchors: use a canonical anchor ID (e.g., anchor:runbook:inference-gateway:cache-stall) so other runbooks can link directly to the proper step.

Dependency matrix columns (minimum):
- service_name, repo, primary_owner, secondary_owner, slack_handle, pagerduty_team, fallback_action, expected_restore_ms, notes
- Capture whether a fallback requires data plane change or only control-plane (important for Private deployments).

Automation ideas (low friction):
- GitHub action to validate that every service has a runbook anchor file in a designated folder (fail PR if missing).
- A tiny Lambda to create an ephemeral collaboration channel with pre-populated pinned runbook and checklist when /handover-start is run.
- A lightweight linter that flags runbook fragments missing contact info or explicit rollback steps.

Drill plan (Week 4):
- Scenario: KV-cache degradation under load causing latency SLO breach for a canary tenant.
- Roles: incident commander (serving-runtime EM), mitigation lead (platform-engineering), SRE observer (Asha), observability checker (Evelyn).
- Measured outputs: time to identify root cause (target < 12 min), time to apply mitigation (< 20 min), time to validate SLIs (< 10 min).
- Post-drill deliverable: annotated timeline and gap doc attached to this pilot.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle cross-region dependencies where on-call is in a different business day? (Need holiday/weekend plan)
- Burden on small teams to create runbooks; need minimal template to reduce friction.
- Privileged automation for creating channels — security review required.
- Ownership drift: how to enforce runbook maintenance (suggest quarterly runbook owner ping).

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Asha: publish initial template (draft) and create pilot Jira ENG-4821 (done).
- Jonah: capture serving-runtime fragments for inference-gateway and kv-cache by 2026-05-21.
- Evelyn: prepare alert-to-SLI mapping extract and share by 2026-05-25.
- Marco: prototype Slack shortcut and share design doc by 2026-06-01.
- Priya: draft customer communication snippet for canary-impact scenario by 2026-06-03.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Consider an "ownership token" pattern: assign a 15-minute token to an individual; they can pass token via the /handover UI to transfer responsibility.
- Possibly integrate with Redwood Console to present the runbook anchor in the per-route dashboard.
- Keep pilot small; focus on model-serving first then expand to embeddings and batch pipelines.

Appendix: templates and examples to copy from (links):
- Runbook template (markdown) -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Runbook+Templates
- Example runbook fragment (kv-cache) -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/runbooks/kv-cache.md
- Pilot Jira epic -> ENG-4821

If you want to edit directly: drop changes in the runbook-stitching branch (git: infra/runbook-stitching) or ping me in #ops-stability.

-- Asha
